learning_outcomes.text: Possess the capacity to design, develop, implement, manage and improve products, systems and processes in different industrial fields, using appropriate analytical, computational or experimental techniques.
Apply the acquired knowledge to identify, formulate and solve problems in broad contexts, being able to integrate them working in multidisciplinary teams.
Communicate knowledge and conclusions, both orally and in writing, to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Incorporate ICT and Industrial Engineering technologies and tools into their professional activities.
Organization and planning of projects and human teams. Teamwork and leadership capacity.
Basic knowledge of industrial production and manufacturing systems.
Basic knowledge of industrial production systems.
Be able to quantitatively model these processes and to estimate the values of the variables that intervene in each case, under different conditions.

syllabus_topics: Calibration of measuring instruments. Uncertainty calculation
Topic 4: Automation of manufacturing processes and NC programming
Introduction to the automation of manufacturing processes
Devices for storage, transport and control
Programming of machine tools with numerical control
Design of parts, runners and risers
teaching_methods: Problem classes, with practical exercises by the professor and/or collaborative activities with student participation.
assessment_rules: The evaluation model allows overcoming the course by progressive, global, or final (extraordinary) evaluation. For progressive evaluation, students need at least 4 points in EP1 (Topics 1-3) and EP2 (Topics 4-6), completion of laboratory practices, and a combined average (NMC = EP1 * 0.4 + EP2 * 0.4 + PL * 0.2) of at least 5 points. Students who do not pass progressively can take a global exam, which has three parts (EO1, EO2, PLO) and similar passing conditions, maintaining the higher grade for equivalent parts. The extraordinary call exam covers the entire syllabus, requiring a minimum of 5 points and completed laboratory practices.
